# Pin labels in an app sidebar

Show the signed-in member's pinned workspace labels under an app's folder list, where one click filters the app through its label URL parameter. Pins are personal; Mail is the reference.

1. The app needs a `label: uuid` parameter in `appViews` (`src/lib/app-view.ts`) and a list that filters by it: Mail and Contacts filter in SQL (`EXISTS` on `mail_tag` or `resource_label`), Chat and Calendar call `labels.Filter(ctx, w, source, labelId)` in the list handler, and Drive filters the listing it already returns with its labels. Never filter only the visible page on the client when the route is paged.
2. Render `<PinnedLabels workspaceId app="<app>" value={view.label ?? ""} onChange={label => set({ label, <open item>: undefined })} />` (`src/components/PinnedLabels.tsx`) inside the app's `AppSidebar`, under its folders. A pinned click pushes a history entry; the label filter select (`ResourceLabelFilter` with `pinApp`) replaces it and offers the pin checkbox. Call `useLabelGuard(workspaceId, labelId, onLost)` so a deleted label leaves the URL with a notice.
3. Pins are `label_pin` rows of the signed-in subject in the workspace (`internal/labels/pins.go`): `app` is one app or `all`, `pinned=false` is an explicit unpin, and a system label (`mail_label.system_key`) is pinned by default in its app without a row. Use the routes under `/api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/label-pins`; a label of another workspace is a 404. Settings → Labels holds a checkbox per app.
4. Test it: a Go test for any new list filter (another workspace's label matches nothing), and an e2e spec at 390px and 1440px with labels and resources unique to the run, as `e2e/label-pins.spec.ts` does. Run `lidza check --json` and `lidza test --e2e`.
